block_05_direct_answer.body_html: A property can suit short-term rental use only when demand, rules and economics all work. Confirm current short-term rental rules and permissions before relying on an Airbnb-style income strategy.

items.answer: A property can suit short-term rental use only when demand, rules and economics all work. For off-plan buyers, check whether short-term letting is permitted for the property and what building, community or licensing conditions may apply.
items.question: Should I buy for Airbnb?

items.answer: Rental demand should be checked through realistic tenant activity, not headline yield claims. Use comparable units, actual leasing evidence and realistic ranges instead of basing the decision only on advertised asking rents.
items.question: How should I assess rental demand?

items.answer: Investment logic should connect the purchase price to realistic income, costs and exit options. Use evidence on tenants, future buyers and competing supply rather than assuming that a strong location guarantees an easy rental or resale.
items.question: How should I assess the investment case?

items.answer: Resale potential depends on future buyer demand, competition and the property’s distinctiveness. Consider selling costs, financing appeal, expected marketing time and any contractual restrictions that could make an exit slower or more expensive.
items.question: How should I assess resale potential?

items.answer: A rental-income area should combine tenant depth with sustainable ownership economics. The investment only works if rent is achieved near the top of current asking levels. Use current listings and transaction evidence before treating any district or property as the strongest income option.
